Hi Rafael,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. We started mapping our firewall policy for the private endpoint and have two immediate asks so we can finalize the change window: 1) we need confirmation of which outbound IPs/tokens the runtime will originate from (control plane vs data plane differences), and 2) whether Redwood will accept TLS interception between our proxy and the runtime (we'd prefer mTLS but we may have an HTTP proxy in front of the NAT).

Specifically:
- We need a short list of cidr/ip ranges (or a deterministic hostname) for the outbound connection to your control plane and for model-serving egress (private runtime).
- Clarify if the Acrobat data-plane connections (token validation, usage telemetry) ever make outbound calls to third-party CDNs that might change over time.
- Any special SNI or ALPN expectations we must preserve through our proxy.

We have a maintenance window Fri 11/12 01:00–03:00 UTC and would like to complete allowlist changes beforehand. Can you confirm by EOD tomorrow?

Hi Jane — thanks for the clear list. Quick answers up front, followed by a short internal note I copied to our network/security folks: 

1) Egress origins:
- Control plane (management calls, metrics, key ops): uses our managed control plane IP pool; those are stable and published; see attached small CSV with the /24 blocks we publish for US region.
- Data plane (model serving from private runtime): by default the runtime will use the customer's NAT egress IP (i.e., origination is from your environment), unless you deploy Redwood-managed outbound proxies (an optional pattern we provide for air-gapped customers).

2) Third-party CDNs: We do not make direct calls to public CDNs for inference traffic. Telemetry and optional feature flags may POST to our control plane which is under the control plane IP blocks; we do not embed dynamic CDN endpoints in the runtime.

3) TLS/mTLS & proxy behavior:
- We support TLS passthrough to Redwood-managed endpoints. For customers using an HTTP proxy that performs TLS interception (MITM), we recommend mutual TLS from your proxy to the Redwood control plane; otherwise token exchange and standard TLS (with SNI preserved) are required.

Action: attaching a CSV with the minimal control plane egress blocks and a short checklist for proxy handoffs. Olga — can you confirm the control plane IP blocks we publish are the same ones in the attached CSV and call out any ephemeral ranges?

Rafael
Rafael Mendes

Rafael / team — confirming items and adding a couple of operational caveats for Acme: 

- The attached CSV contains the stable control-plane /24s for us-us region. There are two ephemeral /32s used during maintenance for failover; we document them in the change log and notify customers via the Console. For allowlisting, prefer the /24s — we rarely add new blocks.
- For private runtime (customer-hosted VPC): the actual inference outbound connection (if any) will appear to come from the customer NAT unless the customer opts into Redwood-managed egress. If Redwood-managed egress is selected, we provide a fixed egress FQDN that resolves to our proxy fleet; customers must allow outbound to that FQDN and to the control plane blocks.
- SNI: SNI must remain intact. Some HTTP proxies strip/replace SNI — that will break TLS validation with our certificates. ALPN: http/1.1 and h2 supported; prefer h2 for control plane.
- Recommendation: for Acme's proxy setup, enable mTLS from their proxy->control plane using the certs we'll exchange via the handshake checklist. If they cannot do mTLS, ensure the proxy preserves SNI and does not downgrade TLS version.

Operational notes to include in the change window:
1) Add control-plane /24s to firewall allowlist.
2) Ensure NAT preserves source IP (for our telemetry correlation).
3) If using Redwood-managed egress, add the provided FQDNs to the proxy allowlist and permit outbound to the proxy's IPs.

I'll attach the handshake checklist (small PDF) that includes the cert exchange steps and sample iptables/proxy config snippets.

—Olga
Olga Petrov
Network Reliability, Redwood Inference

Jane — following up with the consolidated ask and next steps ahead of your Fri window. Summary below and an explicit checklist so your ops team can tick boxes: 

Summary (short):
- Control-plane outbound: allowlist the /24 blocks in redwood-private-egress-sample-ip-list.csv. Those are stable for the US region; we will notify you for any changes.
- Data-plane: by default originates from your NAT (no Redwood egress IPs) unless you opt into Redwood-managed egress; please confirm if you want managed egress (we can enable a staged rollout).
- TLS: preserve SNI and ALPN; prefer mTLS from your proxy to our control plane if you can.

Checklist for Acme ops (copy/paste):
- [ ] Add control-plane /24 blocks from 'redwood-private-egress-sample-ip-list.csv' to perimeter firewall (outbound allowed).
- [ ] If you will not use mTLS, ensure your proxy does not terminate and reissue TLS to our endpoints (preserve SNI).
- [ ] Preserve source IP in NAT for accurate telemetry (do not SNAT behind an additional NAT in front of the proxy).
- [ ] If you choose Redwood-managed egress, add 'egress-us.redwood-inference.com' to proxy allowlist and allow outbound to the IPs returned in DNS.
- [ ] Exchange certs and verify handshake per 'egress-handshake-checklist.pdf' prior to the maintenance window.

Would you like us to join the change window kickoff to validate connectivity? We can schedule a 20 minute gating call.

Best,
Rafael
